summary: Jackson Twp, Ocean County NJ: first new state fire tower in 78 years, dedicated March 2026 at 133 ft, replacing the 1944 Lakewood tower dismantled in 2024.

events.note: Dedicated March 25; built by Fitzpatrick & Associates of Eatontown for about $2 million. Completion date not stated; year inferred from the dedication and the 250th-anniversary wording.
Lakewood Fire Tower (1944) taken out of service in July 2024 and dismantled after its lease expired; this tower replaces it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Shore News headline says 173 feet; the article body and the Pine Barrens Tribune both say 133 feet. The story and facts use 133 feet (40.5 m).

sources.title: State Dedicates 'Veterans Fire Tower', First New Fire Tower in 78 Years
This 173 Foot Tower in Jackson is First One Built in New Jersey in 78 Years

notes_for_editor: Dedication year 2026 is supported by the Pine Barrens article's April 9, 2026 dateline and its 250th-anniversary-this-year wording; the nj.com article returned HTTP 403. The NJ DEP release (dep.nj.gov/newsrel/26-0010/), cited by the OSM note, returned no text, so it is not cited. The NBC10 article failed to load. The OSM note says the location was not confirmed on site. Access, staffing and any fire history are unknown; no access level or staffing key is recorded. The brief record (standing, NJ Forest Fire Service, OSM point) checks out, so no corrections are proposed. Current status is not claimed: the story cites only the OSM entry, which says the location was not confirmed on site, and no longer calls the tower working.
